_meta.purpose: Air-quality context for the eight host cities, thresholds for interpreting measurements, and a slot for measured June-July climatology.
_meta.climatology_status: not populated in this release. Run scripts/refresh_air_quality.py on a machine with internet access to fill 'climatology' from the Open-Meteo air-quality archive (CAMS global reanalysis/forecast). The tools work without it and say so.
caveats: City profiles below are qualitative and describe typical sources and seasonality; they are not measurements.
Reanalysis or satellite-derived values represent a grid cell, not the stadium or training ground; a roadside training pitch can be much worse than the city mean.
Where a state network operates, its stations are the reference measurement; check the agency portal in the weeks before travel.
Brazil's national standards are set by CONAMA Resolution 506/2024 and tighten in stages (PI-2 applies from 1 January 2025); they are less strict than the 2021 WHO guideline levels.

planning_bands_pm2_5_24h_ug_m3._note: Author-defined planning bands for training and match decisions, anchored on the WHO 2021 24-hour guideline level (15 ug/m3) and its interim targets (IT-4 25, IT-3 37.5, IT-2 50). They are not regulatory thresholds and not a clinical standard.

moderate.action: Proceed. Athletes with asthma or exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) should pre-treat as usual and report symptoms; prefer parks or low-traffic routes for easy sessions.

elevated.action: Shift high-intensity outdoor work away from peak traffic hours; consider indoor alternatives for the hardest sessions; check EIB athletes before and after training; ensure reliever inhalers are carried.

high.action: Move high-intensity and long outdoor sessions indoors where possible; shorten outdoor exposure; review asthma action plans; discuss with the team physician before any outdoor session for symptomatic athletes.

very_high.action: Train indoors with filtered air if available; outdoor sessions only if unavoidable and shortened; individual medical review for athletes with airway disease; escalate to tournament medical officers if a match is affected.

asthma_eib.prevalence_note: Respiratory conditions affect roughly 20-70% of elite athletes depending on the sport; EIB is the most common chronic condition in elite sport, and resting spirometry is often normal, so objective testing is needed.
diagnosis: Exercise challenge or eucapnic voluntary hyperpnoea rather than resting spirometry alone
Document the diagnosis before the tournament; symptoms alone over- and under-diagnose
management: Inhaled corticosteroids are the basis of treatment; short-acting beta-2 agonists alone are not adequate control
Extended warm-up before intense work reduces EIB severity
Reduce exposure: avoid peak-traffic hours and roadside routes, and use indoor alternatives when pollution is high
Carry spare inhalers and spacers; check they are in the medical kit for every venue

anti_doping_2026.notes: Inhaled use only, within these 24-hour maxima (salbutamol also not more than 600 ug per 8 h; formoterol not more than 36 ug per 12 h; salmeterol not more than 100 ug per 8 h). Other routes are prohibited. Urinary thresholds apply for salbutamol and formoterol. Check the current list and whether a therapeutic use exemption is needed.

rio_de_janeiro.typical_sources: Road traffic in a dense coastal metropolis, with industry in the wider bay area
rio_de_janeiro.june_july_note: Coastal ventilation is usually good, but calm, stable winter mornings can trap traffic emissions.

sao_paulo.typical_sources: The largest vehicle fleet in South America; traffic-related PM and NO2 dominate
sao_paulo.june_july_note: Winter is the dry season with frequent thermal inversions, the time of year when particulate levels are typically highest.

brasilia.typical_sources: Traffic; regional biomass burning during the dry season
brasilia.june_july_note: Very dry air (mean relative humidity about 51% in July) irritates airways in its own right; dry-season fires in the central region can raise particulate levels.
brasilia.table_label: Very dry air; dry-season smoke possible

belo_horizonte.typical_sources: Traffic, with mining and industry in the metropolitan region
belo_horizonte.june_july_note: Dry winter with light winds; particulate levels are usually higher than in the wet season.
belo_horizonte.table_label: Traffic and industry; dry, light winds

porto_alegre.june_july_note: Humid, often windy and wet in winter, which disperses pollutants; cold, damp air is itself a trigger for exercise-induced bronchoconstriction.

monitoring.agency: FEPAM (Rio Grande do Sul) air quality reports

salvador.typical_sources: Traffic; port and industrial activity in the metropolitan region
salvador.june_july_note: Strong sea breezes and a wet June-July usually keep particulate levels low.

recife.june_july_note: Wettest months of the year with steady onshore winds; good dispersion, high humidity.

fortaleza.typical_sources: Traffic; port and industrial complex to the west of the city
fortaleza.june_july_note: Persistent trade winds give good ventilation; heat and humidity are the dominant environmental problems here, not pollution.
